picks.why: the city’s best-known historic building, in color; no town view exists for this period

picks.what: The new main post office, postcard
picks.why: clear, labeled postcard of a prominent public building; the only usable view before 1955

gaps: P0–P2: nothing; P6: only the Nordsternpark (#10) and views from Bottrop of the Scholven power plant and the stadium (#11–#13), skipped
notes: #1 was painted in 1842 but shows the castle’s north side as it was before 1828, and Horst was a separate village until 1928; drop it if a contemporary town view is required. #2 (Haus Lüttinghof lithograph, 1837–40) is a minor manor house. #4 (Schloss Berge, Buer, about 1900) is mostly pond and trees. #3 is Capri, #8 a Dutch army postcard, #9 an envelope. The 1955 view already covers modern years, so the weak #10 Nordsternpark panorama was not added. #7 keeps the printed caption ‘Gelsenkirchen. – Neue Post.’ in the sky at upper right; cutting it would cut off the tower.
